result.working_check: The student uses $F = ma$ with $a = v/t = 25/5 = 5\ \text{m/s}^2$. This is the correct magnitude of the deceleration, since the car goes from 25 m/s to 0 in 5.0 s. Then $F = 1200 \cdot 5 = 6000\ \text{N}$, which is correct. The question asks only for the magnitude, so the sign and direction are not needed. The final answer of 6000 N (6.0 kN) is correct. The only gap is that the formula $a = v/t$ is not written as a change in velocity, and the student did not say that the force points opposite to the motion.

issues.description: The student writes $a = v/t$ without noting that $v$ is the change in velocity ($25 \to 0$ m/s). They also do not say the acceleration and force point opposite to the motion. The magnitude is still correct.
